# Adjudication Task — Chapter 202

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃202화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|한 식경. 자그마치 30분이다.
  6|
  7|상대가 아무리 화왕이라고 해도 온 힘을 다하면 조금은, 아주 조금은 물러나게 할 수 있을 거라 생각했다.
  8|
  9|방금 전까지는.
 10|
 11|‘이게 말이 되나.’
 12|
 13|나는 질린 얼굴로 물러났다.
 14|
 15|공력에 회전이 가미된 창날을 맨손으로 잡다니. 분쇄기에 손을 집어넣는 것만큼이나 말도 안 되는 짓이다.
 16|
 17|그렇지만 손의 주인공이 화왕 적천강이라면 이야기는 달라진다.
 18|
 19|투두둑. 치이익.
 20|
 21|녹아내린 쇳물이 지면에 닿자 수증기가 피어오른다. 그 모습에 적천강이 혀를 찼다.
 22|
 23|“잡철이라 그런지 생각보다 빨리 녹는군. 이번에 재물도 많이 들어왔을 테니 철 좀 좋은 거 쓰라고 해라.”
 24|
 25|“어, 어떻게 한 겁니까?”
 26|
 27|“너도 할 수 있다.”
 28|
 29|“저도요?”
 30|
 31|“물론이다. 이 갑자 이상의 공력과 본문의 무공을 극성으로 익힌다면.”
 32|
 33|“…….”
 34|
 35|“쉽지?”
 36|
 37|퍽이나 쉽겠다.
 38|
 39|내가 어이없다는 표정을 짓자 적천강이 입을 벌리고 하품을 쩍 내뱉었다.
 40|
 41|“여유 있군. 노부가 네 녀석이라면 그럴 시간에 창이라도 한 번 더 휘두를 텐데.”
 42|
 43|“안 그래도 그럴 참입니다.”
 44|
 45|허공에 떠 있는 제한 시간을 곁눈질하며 새로운 창을 꺼내 들었다.
 46|
 47|남은 시간은 16분. 어느새 절반에 가까운 시간이 지나갔다.
 48|
 49|‘한 걸음. 고작 한 걸음만 물러서게 만들면 되는데…….’
 50|
 51|그게 쉽지 않다.
 52|
 53|나는 처음 그 자리에 느긋하게 서 있는 적천강을 노려보며 크게 숨을 들이켰다.
 54|
 55|“후읍-”
 56|
 57|슈욱!
 58|
 59|동시에 땅을 박차고 달려들었다. 적천강과 나 사이의 거리를 지워 버릴 만큼 널찍한 일 보(步)와 함께 창을 뻗어 낸다.
 60|
 61|쐐애애액!
 62|
 63|그런 나를 보는 적천강의 입꼬리가 솟구쳤다.
 64|
 65|“이제 시작이라고 했을 텐데.”
 66|
 67|쿠궁!
 68|
 69|단 한 번의 발 구름. 그러나 효과는 무시무시했다.
 70|
 71|지진이라도 난 것처럼 땅이 흔들리고 앙상한 나뭇가지에 앉아 있던 새 무리가 날아오른다.
 72|
 73|느려진 세상 속, 순간 흐릿해진 적천강의 손이 허공에 떠오른 수십 개의 돌멩이를 쳐 냈다.
 74|
 75|바로 나를 향해.
 76|
 77|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
 78|
 79|공력을 실어 쏘아 보낸 수십 개의 돌멩이. 그 하나하나가 치명적인 암기나 다름없다.
 80|
 81|분명 과거에 상대했던 대장로의 탄지공(彈指功)보다 더한 파괴력을 지녔을 것이다.
 82|
 83|하지만…….
 84|
 85|‘나도 강해졌어.’
 86|
 87|웅, 웅, 웅.
 88|
 89|창이 울음을 토해 낸다.
 90|
 91|일류에 머무르던 때와는 차원이 다른 일체감이 느껴졌다.
 92|
 93|이미 대성에 이른 진가창법과 보법은 완벽한 합일을 이루었다.
 94|
 95|절정의 벽을 넘어서며 얻은 깨달음이 녹아드니 이전에는 생각할 수 없던 투로가 보인다.
 96|
 97|거기에 상승된 능력치까지.
 98|
 99|‘할 수 있다.’
100|
101|우드득.
102|
103|꽉 움켜잡은 창대가 힘을 견디지 못하고 우그러진다.
104|
105|그리고 다음 순간.
106|
107|화아아악!
108|
109|스프링처럼 응축된 힘이 쏘아졌다. 전력을 다해 횡으로 휘두른 창날의 궤적에서 바람이 뿜어져 나온다.
110|
111|그것은 공력의 발출이었고 내가 불러낸 폭풍이었다.
112|
113|파스스스.
114|
115|고운 가루들이 사방으로 비산했다. 궤적에 걸려든 돌멩이들의 마지막 흔적이었다.
116|
117|“허어, 이놈 보게나.”
118|
119|장애물이 사라졌으니 몸통을 쳐야 할 때다.
120|
121|나는 허탈하면서도 기쁜 표정의 적천강을 향해 달려들었다.
122|
123|쉭! 쉬쉬쉬쉭!
124|
125|공력을 잔뜩 머금은 창날이 허공을 가른다.
126|
127|가볍게 허리를 숙여 피해 낸 적천강의 오른손에서 열기가 솟구쳤다.
128|
129|후웅!
130|
131|동시에 이글거리는 화염이 쏘아졌다. 강력한 열양지기가 응축된 기의 덩어리.
132|
133|나는 이를 악물고 창대를 휘둘렀다.
134|
135|캉! 콰과광!
136|
137|굉음, 그리고 엄청난 힘과 열기가 전신을 덮친다. 온통 새카맣게 그을린 채 서 있는 나를 보며 적천강이 껄껄 웃었다.
138|
139|“이런 무식한 놈을 봤나. 그걸 쳐 낼 생각을 해?”
140|
141|“……후. 거의 다 됐는데.”
142|
143|“웃기는 소리. 노부가 전력을 다했으면 네 녀석은 방금 죽었다.”
144|
145|나는 퉁명스럽게 대꾸했다.
146|
147|“쳐 낼 만하니까 쳐 냈죠.”
148|
149|“그래서 그 모양 그 꼴이냐?”
150|
151|“……이렇게 될 줄은 몰랐지만.”
152|
153|“볼썽사납게 쓰러지지 않은 건 칭찬해 주마. 기어코 막아 낸 것도.”
154|
155|“그런데 막기만 하시는 거 아니었어요?”
156|
157|“누가 그러더냐?”
158|
159|젠장. 생각해 보니 그러네.
160|
161|나는 반쯤 걸레짝이 된 상의를 부욱 찢어 내팽개쳤다.
162|
163|“거, 명색이 화왕씩이나 되는 분인데. 손자뻘 되는 어린놈 상대로 너무 힘쓰시는 거 아닙니까?”
164|
165|“대가리에 피도 안 마른 어린놈이 증조부뻘 되는 늙은이를 상대로 창을 휘둘러? 네가 그러고도 산서잠룡이냐?”
166|
167|“노야께서는 초절정 고수잖아요!”
168|
169|“넌 천무지체잖아.”
170|
171|“아니, 그걸 말이라고 하십니까?”
172|
173|“말이 아니면 망아지냐?”
174|
175|“…….”
176|
177|“뭐, 왜.”
178|
179|까드득.
180|
181|창을 쥔 손에 힘이 들어간다. 나는 뜨거운 숨을 내뱉었다.
182|
183|“후우, 이제 제대로 합니다.”
184|
185|적천강이 새끼손가락으로 귀를 후비적거렸다.
186|
187|“응? 뭐라고? 한 방에 숯덩이가 된 하수의 말이라 잘 안 들리는데?”
188|
189|“…….”
190|
191|와, 극혐.
192|
193|노호검객을 발라 버릴 때만 해도 세상에서 제일 시원한 입담이었는데, 막상 내가 당하니까 속이 뒤집힐 지경이다.
194|
195|“이러다가 제가 정말 한 걸음이라도 물러나게 만들면 어쩌려고 그러십니까?”
196|
197|“차라리 천마가 소림 방장이 되는 게 빠르겠다.”
198|
199|“으득.”
200|
201|“이제 냉수 한 잔 마실 시간밖에 안 남았을 텐데, 그 안에 노부를 물러나게 만들 수 있겠느냐? 어림없지.”
202|
203|적천강의 말은 사실이었다. 남은 시간은 고작 3분 남짓.
204|
205|지금까지 그와 나눈 손속을 돌이켜 보면 퀘스트 실패는 예정된 미래나 다름없다.
206|
207|그러나 내게는 아직 보여 주지 않은 비장의 한 수가 남아 있었다.
208|
209|나는 자연스럽게 대화를 이어갔다.
210|
211|“그러다가 진짜 후회하실걸요.”
212|
213|“후회는 무슨. 애초에 네놈 실력이 어느 정도인지 알아보려고 한 것이다. 그래도 싹수는 제법 보이니 계속 정진하면…….”
214|
215|“아쉽네요.”
216|
217|“응?”
218|
219|의아해하는 적천강을 향해 나는 짐짓 한숨을 내쉬었다. 정말 아쉬워서 어쩔 줄 모르는 사람처럼.
220|
221|“노야께서 아무런 공세도 취하지 않고 막기만 하신다면 충분히 성공할 수 있는데…… 하긴 그런 조건은 없었으니까요.”
222|
223|“노부가 막기만 하면 충분히 물러나게 만들 수 있다?”
224|
225|적천강의 눈이 번쩍 빛난다. 호승심인지, 호기심인지.
226|
227|그의 눈빛에 깃든 정확한 감정은 모르겠지만 반쯤 넘어온 것은 확실하다.
228|
229|나는 그를 못 본 척하며 손을 내저었다.
230|
231|“아닙니다. 못 들은 셈 치세요. 제가 성공해 버리면 노야의 명성에 금이 가지 않습니까.”
232|
233|그 한마디가 쐐기였다.
234|
235|“……이놈 봐라.”
236|
237|묘한 얼굴로 볼을 실룩거리던 적천강이 마침내 고개를 끄덕였다.
238|
239|“속이 뻔히 보이는 속셈이긴 하다만, 오냐. 어디 한번 해보자.”
240|
241|“진심이십니까?”
242|
243|“화왕일언중천금이라는 말도 못 들어 봤느냐? 노부는 한 번 내뱉은 말은 반드시 지킨다.”
244|
245|“……아, 예.”
246|
247|은근슬쩍 앞 글자 바꿔서 표절하는 것 보소.
248|
249|어쨌건 소기의 목적은 달성했다. 나는 반쯤 숯덩이가 된 창을 버리고 세 번째 창을 꺼내 들었다.
250|
251|‘아마 일회용이 되겠군.’
252|
253|하지만 절정 등급 퀘스트를 완료하는 대가라고 생각하면 말도 안 되는 헐값이다.
254|
255|자세를 고쳐 잡는 나를 보며 적천강이 미간을 좁혔다.
256|
257|“혹시 독이나 암수를 쓰려는 것은 아니겠지?”
258|
259|“에이, 그럴 리가 있겠습니까.”
260|
261|나는 싱긋 웃으며 덧붙였다.
262|
263|“사내라면 큰 거 한 방이죠.”
264|
265|고오오옹.
266|
267|45년의 공력을 집어삼킨 창대가 부르르 떨렸다.
268|
269|
270|
271|* * *
272|
273|
274|
275|콰아아아아!
276|
277|거대한 바위가 날아가고 아름드리나무가 뿌리째 뽑혀 나간다.
278|
279|한바탕 폭풍이 휩쓸고 지나간 공터의 중심엔 적천강이 우뚝 서 있었다.
280|
281|정확히 다섯 걸음 물러난 그가.
282|
283|“너, 너…….”
284|
285|적천강은 반쯤 넋이 나간 표정으로 나와 초토화된 주변을 번갈아 바라봤다.
286|
287|방금 전까지만 해도 아름답던 대자연은 온통 꺾이고 뽑힌 나무와 바위들로 흉물스럽게 변해 있었다.
288|
289|이 모든 것이 단 한 번의 찌르기, 일섬(一殲)이 불러온 결과다.
290|
291|“도, 도대체 무슨 짓을 한 것이냐?”
292|
293|“그, 글쎄요. 저도 이 정도일 줄은 몰랐는데.”
294|
295|절정의 경지에 오른 이후 처음으로 써 본 일섬이다.
296|
297|공력까지 비약적으로 상승한 후라 파괴력이 강해졌을 거라고는 생각했지만 이 정도일 줄이야.
298|
299|잘 모르겠다는 내 대답에 적천강이 빽 소리쳤다.
300|
301|“그게 말이 된다고 생각하느냐!”
302|
303|“그러니까요. 와, 진짜 미쳤…….”
304|
305|순간 눈앞이 핑 돌면서 다리가 휘청거린다.
306|
307|모든 힘과 공력을 한 톨도 남기지 않고 쏟아부은 탓에 벌어진 일.
308|
309|비틀거리는 내 몸을 주름진 손이 받아 들었다. 나를 내려다보는 그의 눈빛은 복잡하기 그지없었다.
310|
311|“전후사정은 나중에 들으마. 우선 쉬어라.”
312|
313|그의 말과 동시에 등으로부터 힘찬 기운이 흘러들어 왔다. 필시 적천강이 나를 위해 불어넣어 준 공력일 것이다.
314|
315|태양을 집어삼킨 것처럼 뜨거울 거라는 생각과는 달리, 그의 공력은 따뜻하고 거대했다.
316|
317|그 포근한 온기에 참을 수 없는 졸음이 쏟아졌다.
318|
319|“노, 노야.”
320|
321|“저항하지 말고 몸을 맡겨라.”
322|
323|“……맞죠?”
324|
325|“응?”
326|
327|“제가 이긴 거 맞죠?”
328|
329|“……!”
330|
331|적천강의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다. 이윽고 그가 쉰 목소리로 대답했다.
332|
333|“그래, 노부가 졌다.”
334|
335|“으헤헤헤.”
336|
337|나도 모르게 웃음소리가 새어 나왔다.
338|
339|비록 수많은 제약이 걸려 있었다고는 하나, 천하에서 손꼽히는 고수인 적천강을 물러나게 했다는 것에서 나오는 기쁨이었다.
340|
341|띠링.
342|
343|
344|
345|- 퀘스트, [일보 후퇴]를 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
346|
347|- 퀘스트 보상이…….
348|
349|
350|
351|멀어지는 시스템 알림 소리를 마지막으로, 나는 깊은 잠에 빠져들었다.
352|
353|
354|
355|* * *
356|
357|
358|
359|‘그놈 참. 잘도 자는구나.’
360|

God, I hated this.

[P97]
When he’d been tearing apart the Roaring Fury Swordsman, his banter had been the most satisfying thing in the world. Now that I was on the receiving end, it made my stomach turn.

[P98]
“What are you going to do if I really make you retreat even one step?”

[P99]
“It would be faster for the Heavenly Demon to become the Abbot of Shaolin.”

[P100]
“Grrk.”

[P101]
“You should only have enough time left to drink a glass of cold water. Do you think you can make this old man retreat before then? Not a chance.”

[P102]
Jeok Cheongang was telling the truth. Barely three minutes remained.

[P103]
Judging by how our fight had gone so far, failing the Quest was practically a foregone conclusion.

[P104]
But I still had one trump card I hadn’t shown him.

[P105]
I continued the conversation as naturally as I could.

[P106]
“You’re really going to regret saying that.”

[P107]
“What do I have to regret? I only wanted to see how skilled you were in the first place. Still, you show some promise, so if you continue to work hard…”

[P108]
“That’s a shame.”

[P109]
“Hm?”

[P110]
I heaved a deliberate sigh at the puzzled Jeok Cheongang, pretending to be genuinely disappointed.

[P111]
“If you didn’t attack at all and only defended, I could succeed easily… But I suppose that wasn’t one of the conditions.”

[P112]
“If this old man only defended, you could make me retreat?”

[P113]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flashed. Competitive pride, perhaps, or curiosity.

[P114]
I couldn’t tell exactly what emotion lay in his gaze, but one thing was certain: he had taken the bait halfway.

[P115]
I waved a hand as though I hadn’t noticed.

[P116]
“No. Forget you heard that. If I succeeded, it would damage your reputation.”

[P117]
That sealed it.

[P118]
“……Look at this brat.”

[P119]
Jeok Cheongang’s cheek twitched, his expression difficult to describe. Finally, he nodded.

[P120]
“I can see straight through your little scheme, but fine. Go ahead and try.”

[P121]
“You mean it?”

[P122]
“Haven’t you heard that the Fire King’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold? Once this old man says something, he always keeps his word.”

[P123]
“……Ah. Yes.”

[P124]
He’d even changed the first word and plagiarized the proverb.

[P125]
Either way, I’d achieved what I wanted. I discarded the half-charred spear and pulled out my third one.

[P126]
*This one will probably be single-use too.*

[P127]
But if that was the price of completing a Peak-Grade Quest, it was absurdly cheap.

[P128]
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes as I adjusted my stance.

[P129]
“You aren’t planning to use poison or some underhanded trick, are you?”

[P130]
“Come on. Of course not.”

[P131]
I grinned and added,

[P132]
“A man settles things with one big blow.”

[P133]
Gooooong.

[P134]
The spear shaft trembled after swallowing forty-five years of internal energy.

[P135]
* * *

[P136]
Kraaaaaash!

[P137]
A massive boulder went flying, and a tree as thick as a man was torn up by the roots.

[P138]
Jeok Cheongang stood tall at the center of the clearing, which looked as though a storm had just swept through it.

[P139]
Exactly five steps behind where he had been.

[P140]
“You—you…”

[P141]
Looking half-dazed, Jeok Cheongang stared back and forth between me and the devastated surroundings.

[P142]
The beautiful wilderness from moments ago had become a grotesque landscape of broken and uprooted trees and displaced boulders.

[P143]
All of it was the result of a single thrust—One Annihilation.

[P144]
“W-What in the world did you do?”

[P145]
“Well, I’m not sure. I didn’t expect it to be this powerful either.”

[P146]
It was the first time I’d used One Annihilation since reaching the Peak realm.

[P147]
I’d expected its destructive power to have increased now that my internal energy had grown by leaps and bounds, but I hadn’t imagined anything like this.

[P148]
Jeok Cheongang shrieked at my uncertain answer.

[P149]
“You think that makes any sense?”

[P150]
“That’s what I’m saying. Wow, this is seriously insa—”

[P151]
The world spun before my eyes, and my legs buckled.

[P152]
I had poured out every last shred of strength and internal energy without leaving so much as a speck behind.

[P153]
A wrinkled hand caught me as I staggered. The gaze of the man looking down at me was impossibly complex.

[P154]
“I’ll hear the whole story later. Rest for now.”

[P155]
As he spoke, powerful energy flowed into me through my back. It had to be internal energy that Jeok Cheongang was channeling into me.

[P156]
I’d expected it to be scorching, like swallowing the sun, but his internal energy was warm and vast.

[P157]
Its gentle warmth brought on an irresistible wave of drowsiness.

[P158]
“Old Master…”

[P159]
“Don’t resist. Let yourself go.”

[P160]
“……I won, right?”

[P161]
“Hm?”

[P162]
“I really won, right?”

[P163]
“……!”

[P164]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyelids trembled. At last, he answered in a hoarse voice.

[P165]
“Yes. This old man lost.”

[P166]
“Heh heh heh.”

[P167]
A laugh escaped me before I could stop it.

[P168]
The fight might have come with countless restrictions, but I had still forced Jeok Cheongang—one of the greatest masters under heaven—to retreat.

[P169]
Ding.

[P170]
> **System**
>
> Quest **One Step Back** was completed successfully!
>
> Quest reward…

[P171]
The fading sound of the System notification was the last thing I heard before falling into a deep sleep.

[P172]
* * *

[P173]
*That boy. He certainly sleeps well.*

[P174]
Jeok Cheongang silently watched the sleeping Jin Taekyung for a long while.

[P175]
His strong, open features made him look like an innocent boy, yet also like a young man who had already weathered the world once over.

[P176]
*What a strange boy. What a strange boy indeed.*

[P177]
The longer Jeok Cheongang watched him, the stronger that impression became.

[P178]
He had thought he’d already peeled away one layer of the boy’s shell, only to discover even harder, more dazzling scales hidden beneath it.

[P179]
*A Hidden Dragon.*

[P180]
This young man, sleeping so peacefully that he was even snoring, was a dragon that had yet to obtain its dragon pearl.

[P181]
That only made Jeok Cheongang more curious. How far would Jin Taekyung go? Would he live long enough to see the boy’s true limits?

[P182]
*Especially that final strike…*

[P183]
Jeok Cheongang looked around once more and let out a hollow laugh.

[P184]
Could this really be the work of a young prodigy who had only just passed twenty?

[P185]
He was certain that even the Sword Saint of years past had not been capable of this much.

[P186]
*The Martial God. Perhaps he could have done it.*

[P187]
A martial artist born human, yet called a god. The one person who had ever inspired awe in Fire King Jeok Cheongang.

[P188]
What had he been like in his youth—the man revered not merely as the greatest under heaven, but as the greatest of all time?

[P189]
As Jeok Cheongang imagined Jin Taekyung as he was now alongside the Martial God in his youth, a quiet laugh escaped him.

[P190]
*For this old man to entertain such a thought… The boy’s talent must truly be great enough to compare with the Martial God’s.*

[P191]
Jeok Cheongang gazed deeply at Jin Taekyung, then rose to his feet.

[P192]
By now, a desire was rapidly taking root within him—the desire to place a dragon pearl in the hands of this young Hidden Dragon.

[P193]
*Fly freely above the clouds. Become a Heavenly Dragon capable of covering the world with rain and wind.*

[P194]
Grrrrrk.

[P195]
At the snore that came instead of an answer, Jeok Cheongang burst into hearty laughter.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

The spear shaft trembled after swallowing forty-five years of internal energy.

[P135]
* * *

[P136]
Kraaaaaash!

[P137]
A massive boulder went flying, and a tree as thick as a man was torn up by the roots.

[P138]
Jeok Cheongang stood tall at the center of the clearing, which looked as though a storm had just swept through it.

[P139]
Exactly five steps behind where he had been.

[P140]
“You—you…”

[P141]
Looking half-dazed, Jeok Cheongang stared back and forth between me and the devastated surroundings.

[P142]
The beautiful wilderness from moments ago had become a grotesque landscape of broken and uprooted trees and displaced boulders.

[P143]
All of it was the result of a single thrust—One Annihilation.

[P144]
“W-What in the world did you do?”

[P145]
“Well, I’m not sure. I didn’t expect it to be this powerful either.”

[P146]
It was the first time I’d used One Annihilation since reaching the Peak realm.

[P147]
I’d expected its destructive power to have increased now that my internal energy had grown by leaps and bounds, but I hadn’t imagined anything like this.

[P148]
Jeok Cheongang shrieked at my uncertain answer.

[P149]
“You think that makes any sense?”

[P150]
“That’s what I’m saying. Wow, this is seriously insa—”

[P151]
The world spun before my eyes, and my legs buckled.

[P152]
I had poured out every last shred of strength and internal energy without leaving so much as a speck behind.

[P153]
A wrinkled hand caught me as I staggered. The gaze of the man looking down at me was impossibly complex.

[P154]
“I’ll hear the whole story later. Rest for now.”

[P155]
As he spoke, powerful energy flowed into me through my back. It had to be internal energy that Jeok Cheongang was channeling into me.

[P156]
I’d expected it to be scorching, like swallowing the sun, but his internal energy was warm and vast.

[P157]
Its gentle warmth brought on an irresistible wave of drowsiness.

[P158]
“Old Master…”

[P159]
“Don’t resist. Let yourself go.”

[P160]
“……I won, right?”

[P161]
“Hm?”

[P162]
“I really won, right?”

[P163]
“……!”

[P164]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyelids trembled. At last, he answered in a hoarse voice.

[P165]
“Yes. This old man lost.”

[P166]
“Heh heh heh.”

[P167]
A laugh escaped me before I could stop it.

[P168]
The fight might have come with countless restrictions, but I had still forced Jeok Cheongang—one of the greatest masters under heaven—to retreat.

[P169]
Ding.

[P170]
> **System**
>
> Quest **One Step Back** was completed successfully!
>
> Quest reward…

[P171]
The fading sound of the System notification was the last thing I heard before falling into a deep sleep.

[P172]
* * *

[P173]
*That boy. He certainly sleeps well.*

[P174]
Jeok Cheongang silently watched the sleeping Jin Taekyung for a long while.

[P175]
His strong, open features made him look like an innocent boy, yet also like a young man who had already weathered the world once over.

[P176]
*What a strange boy. What a strange boy indeed.*

[P177]
The longer Jeok Cheongang watched him, the stronger that impression became.

[P178]
He had thought he’d already peeled away one layer of the boy’s shell, only to discover even harder, more dazzling scales hidden beneath it.

[P179]
*A Hidden Dragon.*

[P180]
This young man, sleeping so peacefully that he was even snoring, was a dragon that had yet to obtain its dragon pearl.

[P181]
That only made Jeok Cheongang more curious. How far would Jin Taekyung go? Would he live long enough to see the boy’s true limits?

[P182]
*Especially that final strike…*

[P183]
Jeok Cheongang looked around once more and let out a hollow laugh.

[P184]
Could this really be the work of a young prodigy who had only just passed twenty?

[P185]
He was certain that even the Sword Saint of years past had not been capable of this much.

[P186]
*The Martial God. Perhaps he could have done it.*

[P187]

[P188]

[P189]

[P190]
*For this old man to entertain such a thought… The boy’s talent must truly be great enough to compare with the Martial God’s.*

[P191]
Jeok Cheongang gazed deeply at Jin Taekyung, then rose to his feet.

[P192]
By now, a desire was rapidly taking root within him—the desire to place a dragon pearl in the hands of this young Hidden Dragon.

[P193]
*Fly freely above the clouds. Become a Heavenly Dragon capable of covering the world with rain and wind.*

[P194]
Grrrrrk.

[P195]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 202

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃202화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|한 식경. 자그마치 30분이다.
  6|
  7|상대가 아무리 화왕이라고 해도 온 힘을 다하면 조금은, 아주 조금은 물러나게 할 수 있을 거라 생각했다.
  8|
  9|방금 전까지는.
 10|
 11|‘이게 말이 되나.’
 12|
 13|나는 질린 얼굴로 물러났다.
 14|
 15|공력에 회전이 가미된 창날을 맨손으로 잡다니. 분쇄기에 손을 집어넣는 것만큼이나 말도 안 되는 짓이다.
 16|
 17|그렇지만 손의 주인공이 화왕 적천강이라면 이야기는 달라진다.
 18|
 19|투두둑. 치이익.
 20|
 21|녹아내린 쇳물이 지면에 닿자 수증기가 피어오른다. 그 모습에 적천강이 혀를 찼다.
 22|
 23|“잡철이라 그런지 생각보다 빨리 녹는군. 이번에 재물도 많이 들어왔을 테니 철 좀 좋은 거 쓰라고 해라.”
 24|
 25|“어, 어떻게 한 겁니까?”
 26|
 27|“너도 할 수 있다.”
 28|
 29|“저도요?”
 30|
 31|“물론이다. 이 갑자 이상의 공력과 본문의 무공을 극성으로 익힌다면.”
 32|
 33|“…….”
 34|
 35|“쉽지?”
 36|
 37|퍽이나 쉽겠다.
 38|
 39|내가 어이없다는 표정을 짓자 적천강이 입을 벌리고 하품을 쩍 내뱉었다.
 40|
 41|“여유 있군. 노부가 네 녀석이라면 그럴 시간에 창이라도 한 번 더 휘두를 텐데.”
 42|
 43|“안 그래도 그럴 참입니다.”
 44|
 45|허공에 떠 있는 제한 시간을 곁눈질하며 새로운 창을 꺼내 들었다.
 46|
 47|남은 시간은 16분. 어느새 절반에 가까운 시간이 지나갔다.
 48|
 49|‘한 걸음. 고작 한 걸음만 물러서게 만들면 되는데…….’
 50|
 51|그게 쉽지 않다.
 52|
 53|나는 처음 그 자리에 느긋하게 서 있는 적천강을 노려보며 크게 숨을 들이켰다.
 54|
 55|“후읍-”
 56|
 57|슈욱!
 58|
 59|동시에 땅을 박차고 달려들었다. 적천강과 나 사이의 거리를 지워 버릴 만큼 널찍한 일 보(步)와 함께 창을 뻗어 낸다.
 60|
 61|쐐애애액!
 62|
 63|그런 나를 보는 적천강의 입꼬리가 솟구쳤다.
 64|
 65|“이제 시작이라고 했을 텐데.”
 66|
 67|쿠궁!
 68|
 69|단 한 번의 발 구름. 그러나 효과는 무시무시했다.
 70|
 71|지진이라도 난 것처럼 땅이 흔들리고 앙상한 나뭇가지에 앉아 있던 새 무리가 날아오른다.
 72|
 73|느려진 세상 속, 순간 흐릿해진 적천강의 손이 허공에 떠오른 수십 개의 돌멩이를 쳐 냈다.
 74|
 75|바로 나를 향해.
 76|
 77|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
 78|
 79|공력을 실어 쏘아 보낸 수십 개의 돌멩이. 그 하나하나가 치명적인 암기나 다름없다.
 80|
 81|분명 과거에 상대했던 대장로의 탄지공(彈指功)보다 더한 파괴력을 지녔을 것이다.
 82|
 83|하지만…….
 84|
 85|‘나도 강해졌어.’
 86|
 87|웅, 웅, 웅.
 88|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
